name: Behavior
description: The scenarios a project declares, and where each one sits.

text: What this establishes is that a behavior was read and implemented,
never that the implementation is right. Nothing mechanical can judge
whether the code under a claim does what the claim says, so that one
sentence licenses everything the mechanism cannot check.
The model is Gherkin's, not its file format: these scenarios are read
rather than executed, so `.feature` would buy nothing the other
Of the three disciplines that make one sentence each reachable, the
reason is the one that creeps back into a `then`. It belongs to the
title, and the exit code follows from which of the three the `then`
A scenario nothing claims is answered at the line declaring it because
that is where a reader chooses between writing the test and dropping
the scenario. Both findings collect before reporting, the way a linter
does, so a renamed id is fixed in one pass.

scenarios.title: What the directory declares, and where
given: a behavior directory holding more than one specification
scenarios.then: every scenario answers with the line of the file that declares it

scenarios.title: A directory nobody wrote
given: a behavior directory that is not there

scenarios.title: The root arrives absolute
given: a behavior directory named by an absolute path
scenarios.when: a message about one of its scenarios is composed
scenarios.then: the path answers relative to where the run started

scenarios.title: One id under two scenarios
given: two specifications declaring the same id
scenarios.then: both places the id was declared are named

scenarios.title: A scenario with no id
given: a specification declaring a scenario without an id
scenarios.then: the file is named as declaring a scenario nothing can reference

scenarios.title: A specification that will not parse
given: a behavior specification that is not readable JSON
scenarios.then: the file is named as unreadable

scenarios.title: Several ids on one marker line
given: the text a marker line carries after its keyword, naming more than one id
scenarios.then: each id is answered on its own

scenarios.title: Two scenarios on one line
given: a specification declaring two scenarios on the same line
scenarios.then: both answer at that line rather than the second answering at none

scenarios.title: What each feature's include reaches
given: two features writing different includes over the same directory
scenarios.when: the files each one reaches are taken
scenarios.then: each answers the files its own include covers and no other feature's

scenarios.title: A scenario claimed only from outside its own feature
given: a scenario whose feature includes one file
a claim of it sitting in a file that feature does not include
scenarios.then: the scenario answers as one nothing claims

scenarios.title: The claim that could not witness it
given: a scenario whose feature includes one file
a claim of it sitting in a file that feature does not include
scenarios.then: the claim answers at the line it sits on, naming the specification that declares it
